title: Ben Simmons tears Achilles: Kings guard likely to miss entire season - CBS Sports
description: Simmons, who didn't play during the 2025-26 season, was expected to start for Sacramento this year
body:
Simmons, who didn't play during the 2025-26 season, was expected to start for Sacramento this year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Sacramento Kings guard Ben Simmons tore his right Achilles tendon during practice on Sunday, the team announced. He's now likely to miss the entire 2026-27 season, though the Kings did not put a timeline on his recovery. Simmons, who signed with Sacramento last month on a one-year, $3.5 million deal, was attempting a comeback to play in the NBA again after sitting out the 2025-26 season while rehabilitating from lingering back and leg injuries.Simmons was expected to be in Sacramento's starting lineup on opening night against the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday after starting in the Kings' most recent preseason game against the San Antonio Spurs. Simmons played in two preseason games and averaged 10.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.0 assists. The three-time NBA All-Star was in Sacramento's starting lineup next to Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, Keegan Murray, and Domantas Sabonis, and was starting ahead of DeAndre Hunter, who was acquired by Sacramento at last season's trade deadline.
Simmons had been vocal this offseason about his dreams of a potential NBA comeback before signing with Sacramento weeks before training camp. He traveled to Melbourne earlier this summer to participate in the Australian national team's player-led minicamp, despite not having played for Australia since he was a teenager in 2013.The last time Simmons played in the NBA was during the 2024-25 season, when he appeared in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and the Los Angeles Clippers. During that season, Simmons averaged  5.0 points, 5.6 assists, and 4.7 rebounds.
Before signing with Sacramento, Simmons reportedly had interest from the New York Knicks and the Golden State Warriors, per The Athletic.

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers blasts Buccaneers playing surface after overtime win - CBS Sports
description: Rodgers threw the game-winning touchdown in overtime before calling attention to a field on which he had previous
body:
Rodgers threw the game-winning touchdown in overtime before calling attention to a field on which he had previously suffered two injuries
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After throwing darts during the final stages of the Steelers' come-from-behind win over the Buccaneers, Aaron Rodgers took a shot at Raymond James Stadium's playing surface. Rodgers didn't hold back when asked about the playing surface during his postgame press conference. "It's got to be one of the worst playing surfaces in the league. When we're talking about player safety, that's a real concern," Rodgers said. "I'm thankful I didn't get hurt today, but I've been injured twice on this field before, and in my opinion, the turf was a factor both times. I know USF plays here, but that surface just doesn't feel very safe. From my perspective, it's a field that needs to be looked at because player safety should always come first."  Rodgers' first injury in Tampa occurred in 2008, his first season as the Packers' starting quarterback. He injured his right (throwing) shoulder during a 30-21 loss. The injury did not lead to any missed time for Rodgers, who started in each of Green Bay's 16 games that season. In Week 16 of the 2014 season, Rodgers injured a calf muscle during a 20-3 win over the Buccaneers. Like in 2008, the injury did not sideline Rodgers, who won his second of four league MVPs that season. 
Last year, Rodgers called the Steelers' home field "borderline unplayable" following a win over the Browns in which kicker Chris Boswell lost his footing on an attempted field goal. The Steelers replaced the playing surface before their next game (which had been planned before Rodgers' comments). Raymond James Stadium uses natural grass and shares its field with a local college team. NFLPA president JC Tretter has lobbied for playing surfaces since 2020. In 2022, he called for an immediate ban on specific slit-film turf surfaces. Several teams opted to remove that turf from their stadiums in subsequent fields. 
Rodgers, who threw the game-winning touchdown pass in Sunday's overtime win, is in the middle of his 22nd and final NFL season. Rodgers and the Steelers will now begin preparations for next Sunday's international game in Paris against the Saints.

schema.headline: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers blasts Buccaneers playing surface after overtime win - CBS Sports

title: Champions League Vibe Check: Barcelona, Bayern Munich impress; Manchester United in trouble - CBS Sports
description: Matchday 3's action is headlined by Barcelona's clash with Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal's trip to Bayern Munic
body:
Matchday 3's action is headlined by Barcelona's clash with Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal's trip to Bayern Munich
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The UEFA Champions League will transition into midseason mode this week with several key matchups that will test teams' abilities to make deep runs in this season's competition – or win the whole thing by late spring.Two games in, a few familiar themes are emerging. Back-to-back champions Paris Saint-Germain remain the team to beat while Real Madrid continue to find a way out of trouble, even if wins should feel more elusive to the Spanish giants. Not everyone is in trademark form, though, fascinating subplots emerging as they each begin to chart a way to the podium. Perennial contenders Bayern Munich, for example, hit a stumbling block on Matchday 2 with a 3-3 draw at Viking while Arsenal did not cruise to victory over the weekend.That does not exactly spell bad news for Bayern or the Gunners, the pair amongst a few teams to keep an eye on as the pursuit of Europe's top club prize continues. While they face each other in an all-important clash in Munich on Wednesday, a pair of formidable foes for the title will meet on Tuesday – PSG host a Barcelona side that may have turned over a new leaf. That said, there is bad news for some after a challenging European week, especially as another series of tests awaits.Here's a vibe check heading into Matchday 3 of the Champions League.Every match streams live on Paramount+, your home for every Champions League game all season long, plus replays, highlights, and studio coverage breaking down the race for the top eight. If you haven't signed up yet, now's the time.
Barcelona: Never betterBetween their financial woes and a propensity to concede goals in recent years, Barcelona have been the neutral's problematic favorite. Hansi Flick's side are still a must-watch this season but for all the right reasons, swapping a chaos factor for classic entertainment headlined by Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old is box office week in and week out, following up his pair of assists at Galatasaray on Matchday 2 with a goal and an assist in a 5-2 win at Real Betis on Saturday. The goal is worth watching on a loop, his strike from the edge of the penalty area a reminder that his ability to hit a ball is just as impressive as his creative tendencies. Barcelona are beginning to couple their attacking brilliance, though, with more defensive resolve than they have demonstrated since Flick took over two years ago. They have been serial contenders for the Champions League but more than a decade after they last won it, they might actually be in the best position yet to return to the summit. Tuesday's clash at Paris Saint-Germain will really put that theory to the test.
Bayern Munich: Pretty highVincent Kompany's Bayern Munich resemble Flick's Barcelona in a few ways, including an ability to be lax at the back. They can usually survive blunders at the back because of their sheer attacking might, Ballon d'Or nominees Harry Kane and Michael Olise amongst the most talented and watchable players in the game. It does not mean those defensive errors have not proven costly – Manuel Neuer's risky style ensured they went down early at Augsburg a week ago and only rescued a point out of that game, while their 3-3 draw at Viking on Matchday 2 only added to their overall woes. Bayern, though, have a habit of overcoming those challenges more often than not and responded to two consecutive draws with a 6-1 win over RB Leipzig, a nice confidence booster before Wednesday's clash with Arsenal.Arsenal: Just fineSure, Sunday's 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest was unglamorous and they currently sit three points behind Premier League leaders Manchester City but Arsenal are more or less exactly where they are expected to be at this stage of the season. The likes of Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka may have been stumped by Forest's defense, which is a bit sturdier than the results suggest, but it ultimately was not that much of an issue because of the team's depth. Noni Madueke was able to come off the bench and get the job done, only adding to the intrigue ahead of Wednesday's trip to Munich.
Manchester United: Pretty lowManchester United cannot seem to solve their problems, mediocrity their defining quality even if it should not be. The underlying numbers in the Premier League suggest they should be better than 13th place but their attack sputters constantly and they are just leaky enough at the back to dig themselves into holes frequently. Another imperfect day always feels right around the corner for the Red Devils, no matter the occasion. Wednesday's trip to Como will be worth keeping an eye on for that reason, even if the opponents feel a step below Serie A's elites. The higher-ups may have forced an apology out of him but maybe Lisandro Martinez had a point…
Italian clubs: All-time lowThe number of good days for Italian soccer in recent years is perilously small, one of the sport's most accomplished nations in the midst of a remarkable downward spiral. The two may be intertwined but even outside of Italy's inability to qualify for World Cups, Italian clubs are beginning to struggle at the Champions League level. None of them won on Matchday 2 despite facing a wide range of opponents – Roma were definitely not favored against Real Madrid but let a 3-1 lead slip away, Serie A champions Inter fell to Club Brugge while Napoli could not outdo Villarreal and Como registered a defeat at Feyenoord. Their collective record should be better on Matchday 3 but the margin by which they improve is entirely unpredictable. Inter should be favored against Shakhtar Donetsk and one might pick Roma over Slovan Bratislava. Como might have a nice opportunity in front of them against a shaky Manchester United side but there are no guarantees there, while Napoli will take on a Bodo/Glimt team that's well-positioned to give many teams a hard time.

schema.headline: Champions League Vibe Check: Barcelona, Bayern Munich impress; Manchester United in trouble - CBS Sports

title: Keenan Allen passes Terrell Owens for ninth on NFL all-time career receptions list - CBS Sports
description: The Colts receiver climbed to ninth in NFL history with 1,081 career receptions, and another productive season co
body:
The Colts receiver climbed to ninth in NFL history with 1,081 career receptions, and another productive season could carry him even higher
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There is a new member in the heralded club of the NFL's top 10 career receiving leaders. Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen made eight catches in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans to bring his career total to 1,081. That is good for the ninth most in league history.Allen entered Week 6 at No. 11 on the leaderboard. Cracking the top 10 was not enough for the 34-year-old wideout as he jumped two spots and leaped in front of both Anquan Boldin and Terrell Owens. He now stands a mere 13 receptions behind Tim Brown for eighth place and is on pace to climb even higher than that this season.The vast majority of Allen's career receptions came with the Chargers. His first four years in the NFL were the last four of the franchise's San Diego era, and he moved with them to Los Angeles, where he earned six Pro Bowl selections in seven years. Allen made 70 catches in 2024 with the Chicago Bears before returning to the Chargers last year and adding 81 to his tally.Allen has now accumulated 26 receptions in his first five games as a Colt, which is good for second-most on the team.
The rise up the ladder saw Allen surpass one Hall of Famer, and nearly everyone else in front of him already has or will one day earn a gold jacket. Tight ends Jason Witten and Travis Kelce are the only non-Hall of Famers standing between Allen and the all-time receptions record.NFL career receptions leaderboardRankPlayerReceptions1Jerry Rice1,5492Larry Fitzgerald1,4323Tony Gonzalez1,3254Jason Witten1,2285Marvin Harrison1,1026Cris Carter1,1017Travis Kelce1,096+8Tim Brown1,0949Keenan Allen1,081+10Terrell Owens1,078How far will Keenan Allen climb on all-time receiving list?The Colts will eventually get their No. 1 receiver, Alec Pierce, back from injured reserve. That will diminish Allen's target share, but he should still retain a sizable role in the passing scheme, considering his skill set as a premier route-runner differs from Pierce's threat as a big-play, downfield weapon. At his current pace, Pierce is on track for 83 catches by season's end. That would place him sixth on the leaderboard, presuming Kelce (the only active player ahead of him) does not slip from his own pace.At that point, the question becomes whether Allen will suit up in 2027 and beyond or hang up his cleats for a much-deserved retirement. If he plays one more year, produces at the same pace as he has from 2025-26 (the only stretch of his career in which he was not an every-week starter), and Kelce retires at the end of this season, then he would likely move into the top five.At that pace, it would take five seasons beyond this year to unseat Jerry Rice as the all-time receptions leader.Is Keenan Allen a future Hall of Famer?The company Allen keeps makes it fair to wonder whether he will end up enshrined in Canton, Ohio. The only wide receivers ahead of him on the catches leaderboard are Hall of Famers, and both Witten and Kelce are expected to join the fraternity in due time.There are a couple of other key factors working in Allen's favor. His route-running acumen and ability to move the chains on third down are some of the greatest of his era. And the longevity element works in his favor, too, considering he remains productive into his mid-30s and strung together five consecutive Pro Bowl seasons and another in 2023. Allen was also the Comeback Player of the Year in 2017 when he led the NFL in first downs one season after tearing his ACL in Week 1.A couple of knocks against Allen's resume are critical, though, and could eventually make him the only top-10 career receiver to be absent from the Hall of Fame. The fact that he is a wide receiver presents a challenge, given the extensive backlog at that position on the ballot. Allen does not have a single All-Pro selection; he never led the league in anything besides first downs, and his postseason experience is extremely limited, with just six playoff games played and no Super Bowl appearances.Allen's position on the receiving leaderboard would have to do a lot of heavy lifting for him to separate himself from the other deserving pass-catchers who have been waiting years to get into the Hall.

schema.headline: Keenan Allen passes Terrell Owens for ninth on NFL all-time career receptions list - CBS Sports

title: Meltdown in LA: What went wrong for Rams as Cardinals earn the largest upset of the season - CBS Sports
description: The Rams fall to 2-4 and have a whole host of issues
body:
The Rams fall to 2-4 and have a whole host of issues
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        As Chad Ryland's 43-yard field goal went through the uprights as time expired, the Cardinals capped a wild finish and opened up a whole new set of questions for Los Angeles. The kick, which gave the Cardinals an 18-16 win over the Rams, marked the largest upset of the season. Arizona, which entered as 13.5-point underdogs, also tied for the largest upset of any game in the past five years. It was the largest upset loss of Matthew Stafford's career thus far.The Cardinals, who did not score a single touchdown, led 15-12 with under three minutes left. Stafford led a quick touchdown drive, fueled by big completions to Puka Nacua and capped by a 5-yard touchdown pass to Colby Parkinson with 47 seconds left. Punter Ethan Evans made the extra point after new kicker Blake Grupe got hurt making a tackle earlier in the game. The Rams then kicked off into the end zone — sending the ball to the Cardinals' 35-yard line — and Jacoby Brissett found Jalen Brooks for a 21-yard play on the first play of the drive. Add in a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty on Josh Wallace, and that was all it took to set up Ryland's game-winner.
Give tons of credit to the Cardinals, who earned their first win since the season opener. The maligned defense had a major bounce back after allowing 45 points last week to the Lions, and the offense rolled up 338 yards and scored on six of its 10 drives. Yes, all the scores were field goals, but Arizona's ability to stay on track — Brissett didn't take a single sack and didn't turn it over after the first possession — was key. Arizona had nearly 10 minutes more of possession time than Los Angeles did.
But this is really on the Rams, who are 2-4 after entering the season as the Super Bowl favorite. In fact, it's the same record as the Cardinals.The offense was disjointed, the defense failed to make the big plays, and special teams issues loomed large again.Matthew Stafford not finding explosives — and not really lookingBefore the madness at the end of the game, it looked like this would be the defining play of the game: fourth-and-8, and the Rams do this.
A running back screen — and a failed one at that — in that situation sums up the Rams offense's woeful day. Stafford finished 25-for-33 for 222 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions, but before that, it was an absolute slog: 18-for-26 for just 137 yards. Add in three sacks, and Stafford had a putrid 4.2 yards per attempt.Stafford was getting rid of the ball in 2.50 seconds. He had thrown two deep passes. He was averaging 4.6 yards downfield per throw; for reference, Bo Nix is at 4.9 yards, and that's the lowest number through six games in the past 20 years.In other words, basically nothing in the explosive department. The Rams had only two plays of 20+ yards, and both came on the last drive. Keep in mind this is a defense that allowed five plays of 20+ yards in three quarters against the Lions in Week 5.
There were a few opportunities for big plays — Stafford missed an open Nacua on one notable one — but largely, the quick-passing game appeared planned, and the Cardinals dominated it.More mistakes: Turnovers, penalties loom largeIf big plays aren't on the menu, there's no margin for error elsewhere. The Rams had plenty of mistakes, though. Arguably, the biggest was a Tyler Higbee fumble.
The play before that, Stafford stumbled and fumbled — untouched — when trying to wheel out of the pocket. He recovered the ball, but it set the Rams way behind the sticks on another unforced error. And in another key moment, Los Angeles failed on a fourth-and-1 on a run by backup tight end Davis Allen, a curious play call at best.
The Rams also committed four penalties, three crucial:Byron Young was offside on a third-and-1.Warren McClendon had a false start on the fourth-and-3 that preceded the failed screen pass above.The Wallace penalty set up the Ryland game-winner.The Rams are tied for the 12th-most offensive penalties and tied for the fourth-most defensive penalties this season.Defense can't make playsAfter a Brissett interception on the first drive, the Rams did not have another takeaway. They also recorded zero sacks against a quarterback who's among the more statuesque in the game and an offense down its top offensive lineman (Paris Johnson Jr.) and its top running back (Jeremiyah Love).The Rams have eight sacks all year. Entering "Sunday Night Football" that is tied for the third-fewest in the NFL. And four of those eight came in one game, against the offensively hapless Eagles. Myles Garrett's absence is a major issue, but several other talented pass rushers aren't getting it done.
Special teams issuesGrupe nailed his first field goal attempt, a 44-yarder, in the first quarter. Good news! But the Rams gave up a 40-yard return to Devin Duvernay on the ensuing kickoff, and Grupe hurt his knee making the tackle.
The Rams have now lost games by two, three and four points, and special teams problems have featured heavily in all three. The Grupe injury is out of their control, but it came after they allowed yet another huge kickoff return.Simply put, the Rams have huge problems in all three phases, a truly stunning sentence to type. A team all-in on a Super Bowl just lost to a team that's been counted out for months. Sean McVay's nightmare start continues to get worse.

schema.headline: Meltdown in LA: What went wrong for Rams as Cardinals earn the largest upset of the season - CBS Sports

title: Rams kicker Blake Grupe doubtful to return after suffering knee injury minutes into L.A. debut - CBS Sports
description: Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kickoff
body:
Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on a kickoff
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Los Angeles Rams' kicking conundrum continues into Week 6, but not in the way you'd expect. After cutting former placekicker Harrison Mevis after Week 5, L.A. seemingly found its solution after signing Blake Grupe to assume the kicking duties. The former Notre Dame kicker made his Rams debut on Sunday and quickly endeared himself to his new squad by netting a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter. However, things went downhill after that. After initially being listed as doubtful to return, Grupe has been downgraded to out and will not return to Sunday's contest due to a knee injury, the team announced. Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on the kickoff following his made field goal. He was seen lowering his shoulder to hit returner Devin Duvernay and came down awkwardly. 
With Grupe sidelined, the entire kicking operation is reshuffled. Punter Ethan Evans will serve as the kicker, while receiver Jordan Whittington could be the holder, as ESPN notes he was working on holds along the sideline.
So far, however, the Rams have not called Evans' number to kick. After Matthew Stafford connected with Blake Corum for a 15-yard touchdown in the second quarter, they kept the offense on the field for a two-point attempt, which failed. Then, when they were at the Arizona 27-yard line and faced with a fourth-and-1, Los Angeles went for it, but turned the ball over on downs. Grupe entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2023, initially signing with the Saints. He played for New Orleans until midway through the 2025 season, when he was released. After that, he made stops with the Colts and Jets before finding his way to the Rams. Coming into this game, Grupe had converted 81.9% of his career field goals (86-of-105) and 98% of his extra points (96-of-98). 
The kicking game has been an issue throughout the first half of the season for the Rams, and it came to a head during Monday's overtime loss to the Bills. Mevis failed to convert on either of his field goal attempts, including what would've been a game-winner, which was blocked. That forced Los Angeles' hand to make a change in favor of Grupe, but this latest injury keeps them in a kicking nightmare.

schema.headline: Rams kicker Blake Grupe doubtful to return after suffering knee injury minutes into L.A. debut - CBS Sports

title: AP Top 25: Miami new No. 1, BYU to No. 2; Texas slides in college football rankings - CBS Sports
description: There is a change at the top for the second straight week amid a chaotic weekend of upsets, while BYU's win over
body:
There is a change at the top for the second straight week amid a chaotic weekend of upsets, while BYU's win over Notre Dame earned major respect from the voters
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The wildest Saturday in college football history led to a significant shakeup in the weekly Associated Press Top 25 poll.When five of the eight top-ranked teams all lost on the same day -- the first time in AP poll history -- it guaranteed a new-look top 10. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes are the new No. 1 team in the country, receiving 40 first-place votes. The Hurricanes, atop the AP poll for the first time since 2002, jumped last week's No. 1 Georgia, which slipped to No. 5 after a last-second home loss to unranked Auburn. The Big 12 was the biggest benefactor from Saturday's chaos atop the rankings. BYU jumped all the way up to No. 2 after its controversial win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame. The Fighting Irish fell two spots to No. 4 despite the Big 12 issuing a statement afterward that officials erred in not putting another second on the clock. Texas Tech jumped up two spots to No. 8 after its blowout win over Arizona State. 
The Big 12 now has a conference-best three top-10 teams. The Big Ten also has three top-10 teams (Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA), while the SEC has two. 
        
            
                College football's ranked-win leaders: Teams with the most victories vs. current AP Top 25
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
SEC already eating itselfA week ago, the SEC had four teams in the top 10 and seven in the top 15. This week: Two in the top 10 and five in the top 15. It's no surprise that the SEC is beating itself up, though seeing the Big 12 with more top 10 teams is admittedly eye-opening. The SEC slate is always challenging, and moving to a nine-game conference schedule naturally made it tougher. But Saturday showed just how challenging from top-to-bottom the SEC is this season. The only top-10 team from last week to survive unscathed was Ole Miss. Georgia, Texas and Alabama all went down on Saturday, with two of those losses coming at home. There is no longer an unbeaten team in the SEC, and it sure looks likely there will be more chaos to come within the conference. 
First-year success at UCLA, KentuckyUCLA is a top 10 team. Kentucky is the No. 12 team.In football. Seriously.UCLA's Bob Chesney and Kentucky's Will Stein should be the co-frontrunners for Coach of the Year awards for what they've already accomplished in just half a season. Chesney took over a program that went 3-9 last season and fired head coach DeShaun Foster after only three games. The No. 9 Bruins are 6-0 and ranked in the top 10 for the first time since 2022. UCLA's 17-7 win over Wisconsin without quarterback Nico Iamaleava showed that this team is a legitimate College Football Playoff contender. Stein's situation was a bit better -- the Wildcats went 5-7 in Mark Stoops' last season -- but to be 6-1 in the SEC with wins over LSU, Oklahoma and Texas A&M is beyond impressive. title: Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy suffers injury during Steelers' game vs. Buccaneers - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy spent halftime in the blue medical tent
body:
McCarthy spent halftime in the blue medical tent
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:34 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Instead of spending halftime in the locker room, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy spent it in the medical tent after he sustained an ankle injury at the conclusion of the first half.McCarthy was starting to make his way to the locker room when he started limping and had trouble walking. He was then assisted off the field and into the blue medical tent. He did not speak to the Steelers at halftime.After the game, he revealed he had been stepped on, and that's why he had to go into the blue tent. However, he said he is feeling better. He told the media he delegated much of the halftime head coach responsibilities to assistant coach Joe Whitt Jr. Despite the injury, McCarthy returned to the sideline for the start of the second half. He has also resumed his duties as the team's offensive playcaller. According to the CBS Sports broadcast team, McCarthy twisted his ankle, but it's unclear exactly when or what caused it. 
McCarthy's injury capped off what was a lousy first half for the Steelers, who trailed 13-3 at the intermission. Pittsburgh committed several mental errors in the first half, including Darnell Washington's juggling of an Aaron Rodgers pass, which was ultimately picked off by A'Shawn Robinson. The pick set up the game's first score, a 43-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin. The Steelers' offense gained just 102 yards in the first half. They were just 1-of-6 on third down and 0-of-1 on fourth down. Jalon Daniels, the Buccaneers' undrafted rookie quarterback, dominated the Steelers in the first 30 minutes. Daniels completed nine consecutive passes at one point and recorded the game's first touchdown on a short touchdown pass to Emeka Egbuka. 
The Steelers went on to beat the Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime.

schema.headline: Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy suffers injury during Steelers' game vs. Buccaneers - CBS Sports

title: Week 6 Fantasy Football standouts: Week 7 early waiver wire adds - CBS Sports
description: Jaylin Noel offers big-play upside in Houston, while Isaiah Likely and Chuba Hubbard continue to solidify dominan
body:
Jaylin Noel offers big-play upside in Houston, while Isaiah Likely and Chuba Hubbard continue to solidify dominant roles worth targeting in trades
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season was another wild one with overtime finishes and key Fantasy Football performances that defined the week. Before we turn the page on Week 6, it's time to reflect on key standout performances and what the Week 7 waiver-wire priorities should be. From emerging wide receivers to running backs making the most of expanded opportunities, several players have put themselves on the Fantasy radar. Waiver wire standout of the weekJaylin Noel, WR, Houston TexansWeek 6 stats: 4 receptions, 107 receiving yards, 1 touchdownNoel scored a touchdown last week and showed signs of a budding rapport with CJ Stroud, but an early-week trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. sapped the excitement surrounding Noel during last week's waiver wire. Noel remains unrostered in a slew of leagues and that has to change immediately. Stroud and Noel continue to develop a rapport. Noel, the 2025 third-round pick, is a route winner on the intermediate and vertical levels of the field. Harrison's addition could actually help free up Noel for more opportunities to make big plays. For now, he's probably worth rostering in most leagues, but he's a better fit for non-PPR formats and not a player you should be allocating major budget to.Standout Fantasy performancesIsaiah Likely, TE, New York GiantsWeek 6 stats: 6 receptions, 99 receiving yards, 1 touchdownLikely to continue dominating for the Giants in what has become one of the most concentrated passing games in the entire NFL. Likely is a multi-level route-winner who has consistently uncovered on whip routes and choice routes in the short area while also eating up space and winning matchups in the intermediate range. He's also a monster in the red zone. He is not a sell-high, but more likely a buy-high after proving his production did not slip (and actually improved) once the Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback and benched Jameis Winston. Chuba Hubbard, RB, Carolina Panthers Week 6 stats: 28 carries, 120 rushing yards, 1 touchdown
Hubbard racked up over 100 yards against the Eagles defense and found the end zone. He continues to be one of the best buys in Fantasy Football drafts and likely our biggest league-winning pick of the season. It's the workload that really stands out here. 28 carries in a football game. He's one of the few and true workhorse backs remaining and wouldn't last longer than the second round of Fantasy drafts if we redrafted today. Jonathon Brooks will return at some point, but you have to think this backfield will remain mostly in the hands of Hubbard. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle SeahawksWeek 6 stats: 12 receptions, 134 receiving yards, 16 targetsDefenses simply can't stop JSN despite the lack of other receiving options around him. Teams can and do double-team Smith-Njigba, but his ability to uncover with arguably the best route running in the NFL trumps any coverage defenses will throw at the Seahawks. JSN is a buy high and if you're a Bijan Robinson manager, you might want to consider making a big move to get JSN on your roster.Stock upCaleb Williams, QB, Chicago BearsWilliams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown in Chicago's 31-23 win over Atlanta, and it could've been a much bigger Fantasy performance in his return if some of the rushing touchdowns went his way or if Chicago was forced into a different game script. He picked up right where he left off in Week 1, and let's not forget Ben Johnson told reporters this preseason that he wants to set scoring records. Does Chicago have the personnel to do it? The answer is yes if Williams continues to play like he did this Sunday and in Week 1. He's the best buy at quarterback in Fantasy right now. C.J. Stroud, QB, Houston TexansStroud completed 24 of 34 passes for 312 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Texans' win. He continues to throw with better anticipation and accuracy this season and he looks more comfortable in the offensive scheme than he has at any point since his rookie season. Stroud is likely to get even better as his rapport with Marvin Harrison Jr. improves and, more importantly, as Harrison Jr. 's role in the offense grows. Stroud and Harrison were dominant together at Ohio State. S 
Malik Nabers, WR, New York GiantsNabers finished with 12 receptions for 165 yards against the Saints. He was unstoppable with Jameis Winston at quarterback already over the last two games before this, but his upside looked even greater once McCarthy entered the game. The Giants continue to focus their offense around Nabers and he would be an easy first-round draft pick if we redrafted today. Other early Week 7 waiver wire targetsMichael Penix, QB, Atlanta Falcons: Penix continues to throw the ball with much better anticipation and command in 2026 and he is getting secondary players like Jahan Dotson involved. Atlanta is scoring TDs through the air.Germie Bernard, WR, Pittsburgh Steelers: Bernard benefits from injuries to multiple Steelers WRs ahead of him. His rapport with Aaron Rodgers will continue to improve. He is a borderline weekly FLEX play.Omar Cooper Jr., WR, New York Jets: Cooper's production will be less predictable but his big-play ability is obvious. The former first-round pick is worth a bench stash on talent and upside alone.Demario Douglas, WR, New England Patriots: Douglas continues to produce and not just on short-area targets. He also appears to be a favorite in the red zone. That's a recipe for scoring Fantasy points. Jahan Dotson, WR, Atlanta Falcons: Dotson is reviving his career with Penix and Atlanta and has emerged as a weekly big-play threat.Tyrone Tracy Jr., RB, New York Giants: The Giants can't decide who to play at RB, but Tracy scored two touchdowns and took over the no-huddle passing-downs role again in Week 6. He is the most explosive option in the backfield and is worth rostering in deeper leagues.

title: NFL Week 6 overreactions: Time for Colts to clean house? A.J. Brown trade a mistake by Patriots? - CBS Sports
description: The battle between two of the NFL's most woebegone franchises lived up to its lack of hype Sunday. In fact, in terms of excitement, it m
body:
The battle between two of the NFL's most woebegone franchises lived up to its lack of hype Sunday. In fact, in terms of excitement, it more than lived up to it. But the on-field product was a special sort of fun-bad.Titans 26, Colts 20. It's the first win of the year for Tennessee, and a stunning one at that. The Titans trailed 13-0 at halftime and looked completely lifeless. Bench Cam Ward? Throw in the towel? It seemed on the brink.And then the Colts, being the generous team they are, quite literally gave it away over the next four possessions:Jonathan Taylor fumbled on the first play of the second half. The Titans turned that into a field goal.With the Colts in scoring range on the next drive, Daniel Jones threw an atrocious interception. The Titans turned that into another field goal.The Colts then went three-and-out and gave up a 58-yard Chimere Dike return, setting up the Titans for their lone offensive touchdown of the day.On the next drive, Julius Chestnut blocked a punt, and Oluwafemi Oladejo recovered the loose ball and scored a touchdown.From up 13-0 to down 20-13 in about 18 minutes of game time. Horrifying stuff. The Colts actually tied the game on a Taylor touchdown, only for the defense to commit an awful pass interference to set up a Titans field goal. Tennessee tacked on another field goal late.
A collapse in all three stages? Against a winless team? For an organization already skating on thin ice? Check, check, check. Which leads me to say ...Shane Steichen won't last the season, and Chris Ballard and Daniel Jones will be gone between now and Week 1, 2027Overreaction or reality: RealitySince 2020, there have been 16 in-season coaching changes. Shane Steichen will either be the next or, at the very least, join that list.This was an unacceptable collapse. The Titans are completely inept offensively. The only way they could do anything was if the Colts blew it, and the Colts blew it over and over again. I've generally been a proponent of Steichen as a good offensive mind, but as a head coach, you have to be more than that. You are responsible for everything, and in that matter, Indianapolis isn't close to good enough.
Steichen can't play the game, though, so we turn to the players ... and the person who chose them. Chris Ballard is in his 10th season as Colts GM. The team has one playoff win over that span, and it was back in 2018, his second year. He has been completely unable to find a quarterback, and his latest attempt is turning out as bad as the others.Remember, at the start of Ballard's tenure, he had Andrew Luck. Andrew Luck retired ahead of the 2019 season. It's been that long. Inexcusable. He has tried half-measures with veterans. He tried drafting one (Anthony Richardson). He has failed in every measure. The defense remains iffy at best, even after the blockbuster (and, in retrospect, misjudged) Sauce Gardner trade.But really, it all comes back to Jones: He was 22-for-42 for 269 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. He took six sacks. He's tied for the NFL lead in turnovers. Sunday, he simply did not put an NFL-caliber product on the field.
Remember, the Colts signed him to a two-year, $88 million deal over the offseason, even though they were bidding with ... no one. There is an out after this year that would carry $35 million in dead cap, but continuing with him would be even more punitive for a franchise long overdue for a reset.Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is known for standing on the sideline and keeping notes. Her only notes needed from Sunday? It's time to clean house.The Rams won't make the playoffs playing like thisOverreaction or reality: RealityThis is simply a non-playoff team right now. Here are the stunning numbers from the Rams' stunning 18-16 loss to the Cardinals:
As a 13.5-point favorite, Matthew Stafford suffered the largest upset of his career. It's also tied for the largest upset in the NFL in the last five years.The Rams had zero plays of 20+ yards across their first nine possessions Sunday.Stafford's average pass traveled 4.8 yards downfield, the fourth-lowest number of his Rams career and his lowest since 2024. For reference, the lowest air yards per attempt this year is 4.9, belonging to Bo Nix.The Rams did not sack Jacoby Brissett and are tied for the third-fewest sacks in the NFL this season.The Rams are the fifth preseason Super Bowl favorite in the last 50 years to be under .500 through six games.The Rams have won the turnover battle once in six games this season. And they lost that game -- to the Bills last week -- anyway.Sean McVay summed it up aptly: "There's nothing positive that I can say about today."The offense has very little juice, outside an occasional excellent play by Puka Nacua or Davante Adams. It just feels really stagnant; Stafford used play action on 37% of his dropbacks last year and averaged 8.4 yards per pass on those throws. This year, it's down to 25% and 7.2, respectively. And when a team doesn't have juice, it has little room for error. But the Rams keep making errors: penalties, turnovers, missed assignments, etc.Meanwhile, the defense just isn't causing much havoc. And the special teams issues remain. New kicker Blake Grupe got hurt in the first quarter, forcing the Rams to adjust on the fly.
Even if the Rams had won, it's not close to good enough. Sean McVay said as much. If they lose in Week 7, it's officially panic time.We found an alien lifeform, and his name is Josh AllenOverreaction or reality: Reality
No words needed.The Browns or Steelers will win the AFC NorthOverreaction or reality: OverreactionWell, well, well, if it isn't a three-way tie atop the AFC North through six weeks?! The Browns, Steelers and Ravens are all 4-2, and the Bengals (on bye this weekend) aren't far behind at 3-2.Cleveland technically leads the division thanks to Sunday's 13-10 win over Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore, and Pittsburgh is second because it has a better in-division record.
Sorry, Browns and Steelers fans, but neither one of you is winning the division. Cleveland's largest win this season is by four points. It lost to the Jets just last week. Deshaun Watson looked awful Sunday. The Steelers looked similarly awful, needing a late comeback to force overtime against the Baker Mayfield-less Buccaneers. As it turns out, playing against backup quarterbacks is very helpful.Both teams rank in the bottom half of most major offensive stats. The quarterback play simply isn't good enough and won't be good enough, especially when put up against Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow rather than Tyler Huntley and Jalon Daniels.Patriots made a mistake trading for A.J. BrownOverreaction or reality: OverreactionA.J. Brown's grand return from IR was ... not so grand. Three catches for 27 yards on 10 targets. Officially, he's been charged with two drops. Unofficially, given his high standards, it was probably more. He even bobbled away a Jets onside kick, but lucky for him, a teammate recovered to clinch the Patriots' 26-19 win.
It's worth being concerned about the debut, but to say the trade is a bust or a mistake would be a drastic overreaction. Yes, it's been a tough start with the injury and the underwhelming return. But let's not write it off. He won on the routes New England brought him in to win: quick in-breakers and deep balls. Drake Maye missed him on one of each, and Brown failed to finish other opportunities he did have. It sounds like a silly thing to say, but if you cut the tape right before the ball arrives, Brown's film would look encouraging.Of course, he has to make the plays that are there. Getting open doesn't gain yards, score points or win games. Brown will bounce back, and he can still be a huge boost. He came back from his high ankle sprain earlier than expected. Let's give him a week's worth of grace.C.J. Stroud will be a top-five highest-paid quarterback this offseason ... and deserves itOverreaction or reality: RealityAnother week, another outstanding performance for C.J. Stroud. The fourth-year pro threw for 312 yards, three touchdowns and an interception and led the game-winning drive in the Texans' 34-31 win over the Jaguars.
The numbers are one thing, but the film is just as good, if not better. This is one of the best throws you will see all season.
So is this one ...
This is Stroud at his best: laser-accurate, huge arm, can access every part of the field. It's been missed the past few years, and the Texans should be very glad it's back. Not only that, but he is improving at mitigating negative plays. His interception Sunday was really bad, but it was his first all year. He's also taking fewer devastating sacks than he did last season. And he's doing it all while still not having much of a run game.The Texans and Stroud didn't reach an extension in the offseason. He had been awful in the playoffs, and while both sides said the right things, no agreement happened.
He is very much on the way to earning that massive extension this offseason, though. This offseason is setting up to be a huge one for quarterback deals — Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye and Bo Nix from the 2024 class, Bryce Young from Stroud's 2023 class and Lamar Jackson are all looking for a new deal. Stroud's deal will put him among the top five highest-paid quarterbacks, and it will be well-deserved.Brad Idzik will be a hot head-coaching candidate in 2027Overreaction or reality: RealityThe Panthers topped the injury-battered Eagles 25-14 in straightforward fashion. Bryce Young threw a pair of touchdown passes, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and a score. Philadelphia was without Jalen Hurts, its top three running backs and a bunch of other players. It's not a super notable result by any measure.But Philadelphia still has a really good defense, and Brad Idzik flashed excellent play calling, including on both touchdowns to Tommy Tremble.
I was also super impressed by Young's work on RPO throws, something Idzik and Young have worked into this offense really well.Idzik took over calling plays from Dave Canales this offseason. It has been a perfect promotion. Carolina has one of the most aggressive offenses in the NFL in terms of passing rates. It's a really well-designed offense that empowers Young and accentuates his strengths. In an NFL that loves young, innovative play callers, Idzik is part of the next wave of hotshots.

The Tampa Bay Rays got another dominant start out of Drew Rasmussen on Sunday and a 3-1 Game 5 win put them back up in the ALCS over the Cleveland Guardians. The Rays got to Parker Messick early and drove him out of the game after just two innings. The Cleveland bullpen kept them quiet from there, but it was too late. title: Jameis Winston benched: J.J. McCarthy sparks Giants, but thrilling, historic comeback falls just short - CBS Sports
description: McCarthy helped New York score 17 unanswered points before ultimately coming up just short
body:
McCarthy helped New York score 17 unanswered points before ultimately coming up just short
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It could be the beginning of a new era in New York, as the Giants benched quarterback Jameis Winston for J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter of their eventual 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints. While McCarthy threw an interception on his third passing attempt, he rebounded to spark the Giants and made his case to be John Harbaugh's new starter.In all, McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception in his first extensive action with his new team. In 11 minutes of action, he would throw for 243 yards, which made NFL history for the most passing yards in an 11-minute span. He also led the Giants in rushing with 26 yards. Following his interception, McCarthy led a six-play, 52-yard drive that was capped by a Tyrone Tracy Jr. touchdown and a successful Isaiah Likely two-point conversion to trim the deficit to 16 points. After a Saints three-and-out, McCarthy took the Giants offense 73 yards down the field on just three plays, and hit Likely for a 24-yard touchdown to make it a 10-point game. 
McCarthy was given the opportunity to lead a game-tying or game-winning drive with 57 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter with zero timeouts. On first down, he scrambled up the middle for 28 yards to get the Giants into enemy territory, and then hit Likely for 20 yards to get New York to the Saints' 23-yard line. The Giants eventually faced a fourth-and-1 14 yards from the end zone with 12 seconds remaining, and McCarthy could not connect with Likely in the end zone. The Giants wanted a flag on this play, but the officials held onto their yellow handkerchiefs. 
This was a performance good enough for McCarthy to unseat Winston permanently. Last month, the Giants traded a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for McCarthy. The former No. 10 overall pick went 6-4 as the starter for the Vikings in 2025, completing 57.6% of his passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He became the only first-round pick at quarterback since 1970 to finish last in completion percentage and TD-INT ratio in their debut season. 
Harbaugh said after the game he can't answer who his starting quarterback will be moving forward, and that those are not issues decided 10 minutes after a game. 
It's called the "Jameis Winston experience" for a reason. Last week in the tie vs. the Washington Commanders, he completed 33 of 54 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns. Winston actually became the first Giants quarterback to throw three touchdowns in back-to-back games since Eli Manning in 2016. However, his performance on Sunday opened the door for Harbaugh to consider his other quarterback. Winston completed 14 of 26 passes for 152 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions before his benching.

title: College football odds, lines, schedule for Week 8: Texas favored vs. Ole Miss - CBS Sports
description: Initial odds for college football's top Week 8 matchups are out
body:
Initial odds for college football's top Week 8 matchups are out
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Two weeks away from the first set of College Football Playoff rankings coming out of the wildest Saturday across the sport in decades, the 2026 season has delivered in a big way so far.For the first time in the 90-year history of the AP poll dating back to 1936, five of the top seven teams lost on the same afternoon, sparking a much-needed rebound opportunity for the perceived elites in Week 8. While next weekend's matchups within the top 25 fail to offer a litany of "good on good" games like last, the unpredictability of the sport this season continues to carry significant weight.The only unbeatens remaining at midseason are BYU, James Madison, Miami, Texas Tech, UCLA and Utah after most of the unblemished went down on Saturday. Could more fall in Week 8 to unranked foes?Let's take a look at the schedule and early lines.Odds via FanDuel Sportsbook.
The big gamesNo. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas (-3.5): Will the Longhorns rebound as a home favorite against the Rebels, or will Steve Sarkisian lose a third straight SEC game and bring more questions to the Forty Acres this season? It benefits Texas if defensive end Colin Simmons, who leads the country with 10.5 sacks, returns after being carted off against Florida, but his injury status remains unknown. Trinidad Chambliss is the SEC's top individual playmaker at quarterback and has already had his way against two nationally-ranked opponents this fall with impressive wins over LSU and Missouri.No. 6 Indiana (-7.5) at Michigan: Backup quarterback Tommy Carr provided an immediate spark for the Wolverines against Penn State, leading multiple second-half touchdown drives after being plucked from the bench ahead of Bryce Underwood. Manufacturing that same level of success against the defending national champions, who saw their nation-leading 22-game winning streak snapped vs. Ohio State, is a different task entirely. Indiana hasn't won at Michigan Stadium since 1967, which is perhaps why this opening line seems a bit on the low side.No. 11 Tennessee (-2.5) at South Carolina: Can Shane Beamer knock off another top-15 SEC opponent with the Gamecocks? He's had an extra week to prepare -- 3-4 overall at South Carolina in that spot -- for what the Vols bring to Williams-Brice Stadium in a pivotal matchup for Tennessee's lasting CFP hopes. The Gamecocks clicked for the first time all season offensively last time out at Florida after LaNorris Sellers accounted for five total touchdowns. These two have split their last eight meetings dating back to 2016.No. 14 Houston at No. 10 Utah (-5.5): The Utes survived a Big 12 warning shot at Colorado on Saturday night and now get a red-hot Cougars squad hoping to occupy one of the conference's multiple seats at the CFP table. Houston held off Oklahoma State, 35-32, in Week 7 behind Conner Weigman's five touchdown passes. For Utah, protecting home turf means preserving its unbeaten record and strengthening a playoff résumé that needs its first quality win with BYU looming on Nov. 7.
No. 18 LSU (-6.5) at Auburn: Alex Golesh and the Tigers just knocked the SEC's king off the throne and now comes the tricky part: doing it again at home with everyone paying closer attention. LSU's coming off a 31-point demolition of Mississippi State and knows the margin for error is near zero the rest of the way in SEC play. Was Auburn's win between the hedges a turning point for the program or this season's signature moment? We'll know more after Week 8 inside Jordan-Hare.Best of the restPittsburgh at No. 1 Miami (-22.5)Texas A&M at No. 13 Alabama (-15.5)No. 2 BYU (-7.5) at UCFNo. 8 Texas Tech (-11.5) at CincinnatiMichigan State at No. 9 UCLA (-12.5)Vanderbilt at No. 12 Kentucky (-11.5)Oklahoma (-2.5) at Mississippi StateNo. 15 Iowa (-5.5) at MinnesotaColorado at Oklahoma State (-13.5)No. 16 USC (-2.5) at WisconsinNo. 21 Boise State (-13.5) at Washington StateCalifornia at No. 23 SMU (-17.5)Rutgers at No. 24 Northwestern (-15.5)

title: Josh Allen delivers possible NFL play of the year with improvised TD pass for Bills - CBS Sports
description: Allen avoided a potential sack and improvised an extraordi
body:
Allen avoided a potential sack and improvised an extraordinary touchdown pass that immediately drew comparisons to a legendary Brett Favre play
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 18, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:45 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        It may only be Week 6, but Josh Allen made what could end up the NFL's play of the year during the Bills' win over the Raiders. Allen extended Buffalo's lead in the second half after making one of the most jaw-dropping touchdown passes in recent memory. On the play, Allen stepped up in the pocket and evaded a possible sack before stepping up and flipping a backhanded pass to wideout Keon Coleman.The play had historical significance as Allen tied Hall of Famer Jim Kelly for the most touchdown passes in franchise history. 
Allen's play immediately conjured memories of a similar play made 30 years earlier by another great quarterback, Brett Favre (that play appears at the 5:23 mark in the video below). 
Favre's incredible play against the Rams came during the second of his three consecutive MVP seasons. That was also the season where Favre helped lead the Packers to the franchise's first title in 29 years. 
Allen would undoubtedly love to have a similar outcome this season for himself and for his team. The league's MVP in 2024, Allen is the current front-runner to win the award again this year. Through the season's first five games, Allen scored 15 touchdowns that included a whopping eight touchdowns on the ground. In Buffalo's Week 5 win over the Rams, Allen moved into 16th on the all-time rushing touchdown list. Allen's 87 career touchdown runs are 12 more than the next-closest quarterback, Cam Newton. 
While his play on Sunday was reminiscent of Favre's, Allen would undoubtedly love to mimic another Hall of Fame quarterback by season's end. If he can win a Super Bowl this season, the 30-year-old Allen would do so 20 years after Peyton Manning captured his first title during his age-30 season.

body:
After a 2-5 start and another defensive collapse, Locksley made a change entering Maryland's bye week in hopes of turning the season -- and his trajectory -- around

        Maryland fired defensive coordinator Ted Monachino on Sunday after the defense struggled again in the Terrapins' 37-30 loss to Rutgers.Maryland's defense hasn't lived up to expectations in what has been a disappointing 2-5 start to the Terrapins' 2026 campaign. Maryland currently ranks 83rd in total defense, 84th in pass defense, 85th in rush defense and 127th in scoring defense. "I appreciate Ted's hard work and dedication to our program during his time in College Park," Maryland coach Mike Locksley said. "As I evaluate our program, I believe this change is necessary. We wish Ted all the best moving forward."The decision comes as Locksley's long-term job status is also very much in doubt. After going 4-8 in 2024 and 2025, Locksley entered the 2026 season needing to win around seven games or better to keep his job headed into 2027. Following another blown opportunity against Rutgers on Saturday, the odds of that happening have plummeted. Locksley hasn't beaten a Power Four opponent in more than a calendar year and has a 2-20 Big Ten conference record since the 2024 season. 
There may not be a coach on a hotter seat in college football than Locksley. While there has been considerable outside speculation on Locksley's job security, including whether he'd be fired headed into the open week, Maryland has taken a patient approach in evaluating the situation. Letting Locksley fire Monachino to try to improve the defense headed into a bye week is another example of that. Monachino had been Maryland's defensive coordinator the last two seasons after arriving from North Carolina. The veteran defensive coach had also previously worked for the Baltimore Ravens, Indianapolis Colts, Atlanta Falcons and Jacksonville Jaguars. Co-defensive coordinator Aazaar Abdul-Rahim will take over defensive play-calling responsibilities as Maryland's interim defensive coordinator. Abdul-Rahim, who coaches the cornerbacks, is on his second stint at Maryland after previously working for D.J. Durkin. Inside linebackers coach Zac Spatival will also add the co-defensive coordinator title. 
Maryland has a bye this week before a Halloween home game against Illinois.
